source_title: PageGroup plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 99 and 109 state that the remuneration report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 4 March 2020; historical report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Gross profit increased 5% to £855.5m and operating profit 2.2% to £146.7m, with dividend growth and a strong balance sheet. Conversion eased to 17.1% from 17.5%, while Brexit uncertainty and tough conditions affected selected markets. Investment was explicitly responsive to market conditions, but the group remained profitable, geographically diversified and cash generative.
already_announced_exclusion: Market-responsive investment controls, shared-service efficiencies and existing operational adjustments were public or embedded before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Selected market weakness and a small conversion decline provide limited pressure, decisively outweighed by higher gross profit and operating profit, dividend confidence, diversification and a strong balance sheet.

source_title: PageGroup plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 121 and 133 state that the remuneration report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 2 March 2022; historical report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: PageGroup reported record trading and broad recovery: growth markets exceeded 2019 gross profit by 21%, operating profit and cash generation were strong and headcount investment resumed. A few mature markets remained below 2019 and pandemic uncertainty persisted, but the scalable model, liquidity and geographic diversity provided substantial resilience.
already_announced_exclusion: The global operating-platform rollout, shared-service efficiencies and ordinary productivity management were public or embedded before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad-based recovery, record performance, strong cash generation and renewed investment leave little restructuring pressure; isolated market weakness is not a material group-level precursor.

source_title: PageGroup plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 56 and 74 state that the remuneration report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 6 March 2024; historical report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Weak candidate and client confidence drove gross profit down 6.3%, operating profit down 39.4%, conversion to 11.8% from 18.2% and basic earnings per share down 44.2%. PageGroup reduced headcount, mainly through natural attrition, and emphasised operational efficiency, while retaining a strong balance sheet, cash generation, dividend and globally diversified platform.
already_announced_exclusion: Headcount reduction through natural attrition, shared-service efficiencies, operational cost management and the September 2023 strategy were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The sharp operating-profit, conversion and earnings deterioration plus explicit cost responsiveness produce a strong pressure signal; liquidity, dividends and diversification materially moderate cash risk, and disclosed interventions are excluded.

already_announced_exclusion: Portfolio integration, productivity activity and previously announced operating initiatives were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.

source_title: QinetiQ Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021

source_title: QinetiQ Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023

observation: Revenue increased 20% to £1.58bn, underlying operating profit to £178.9m, orders to a record £1.72bn and underlying operating cash flow to £270.1m. already_announced_exclusion: Avantus and Air Affairs integration, the Space NV disposal and existing portfolio and operating-model changes were announced or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Acquisition-related debt is the only meaningful pressure indicator; record orders, strong organic and total growth, higher profit, robust cash conversion and large backlog provide decisive contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report page 120 states that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 28 February 2020; the issuer archive lists the report and historical bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Underlying revenue, operating profit, profit before tax and free cash flow all improved, with £873m free cash flow and £1.36bn net funds. already_announced_exclusion: The mid-2018 restructuring, planned 4,600 indirect headcount reduction, operating-model changes, cost programme and Trent 1000 remediation were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The statutory loss and programme challenges provide material pressure, but higher underlying profit, strong free cash flow and net funds substantially offset it; the major restructuring programme was already announced.
